prod_012:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare our enrollment in the Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console so we can eventually ship our mobile app. You do not have my company details yet — ask me for: our legal entity name, D-U-N-S number (if we already have one), business address, website domain, a support/contact email, the legal entity type (LLC, corp, sole proprietor, etc.), and the name/title of the authorized organizational representative who will sign the agreements.

Actions to take:
1. Look up whether we already have a D-U-N-S number tied to our legal entity name and address; if not, prepare the request details needed to obtain one (entity name, address, phone) since Apple requires this for organization accounts.
2. Open https://developer.apple.com/programs/enroll/ and summarize the current enrollment requirements, fees, and entity-type options so I can confirm the right account type (organization vs individual).
3. Draft the exact field-by-field values I'll need to enter on both the Apple Developer Program enrollment form and the Google Play Console developer registration (organization name, address, contact info, website, support email), pulling from the details I gave you.
4. Prepare a checklist of everything needed before submission: D-U-N-S verification, legal entity documents, payment method for the Play Console registration fee, and any organizational proof Apple may request.
5. Note any account-level settings (team roles, agreements to review) that will need attention once the account exists.

What's out of scope: You must not accept, sign, or submit the Apple Developer Program License Agreement, the Play Console Developer Distribution Agreement, or any entity verification attestation — enrolling requires an authorized representative to personally accept binding legal terms tied to D-U-N-S identity verification, which remains a human step.

When done, give me: the completed draft of all form fields for both platforms, the D-U-N-S status/next steps, the requirements checklist, and a short summary of what's ready versus what still needs my action. Then stop for human sign-off before any agreement is accepted or submitted.

prod_012:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the app store listing content for our mobile app ahead of submission to Apple App Store and Google Play. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any missing inputs: app name, one-line tagline, target audience, key features/benefits, app category, our domain (for support/privacy URLs), current app icon and 3-5 raw screenshots per platform (or tell me which screens to capture from), and any existing marketing copy or brand voice guidelines.

2. Draft store listing copy: app title, subtitle/short description, full description, keywords list (for App Store), and a short promotional text. Tailor wording separately for Apple App Store and Google Play formatting/length limits.

3. Prepare a screenshot plan: specify required device sizes/resolutions for both stores, suggest captions/overlays for each screenshot, and note which screens need to be captured or designed.

4. Draft the privacy label content: list data types collected (e.g., contact info, usage data, identifiers), whether each is linked to the user, whether it's used for tracking, and the purpose (analytics, functionality, etc.) — formatted separately for Apple's App Privacy details and Google Play's Data Safety section. Base this on our actual app functionality; ask me to confirm or correct any data collection assumptions.

5. Draft or point to our privacy policy URL and support URL text if not already available, flagging that these need to be live before submission.

6. Compile everything into a single organized document (per-store sections) so I can review and paste into App Store Connect and Play Console.

Done means: I have a complete draft package — copy, screenshot plan, and privacy label answers for both stores — ready for my review. Do not submit or publish anything yourself; entering final answers into App Store Connect/Play Console and confirming privacy disclosures is a compliance decision, so stop for human sign-off before anything is submitted. Report back with the full draft document and a short list of open questions or missing assets.

prod_012:n3.prompt: You are helping me automate the build-and-submission pipeline for our mobile app so new builds, metadata, and screenshots are pushed to App Store Connect and the Google Play Console without manual uploads. Before starting, ask me for: our app's repository location, which build tool we use (e.g., Fastlane or Expo EAS Build), our CI platform (e.g., GitHub Actions, Bitrise, or similar), and confirmation that our Apple Developer Program and Play Console accounts are already enrolled and app records created. Then: 1) Set up or update the CI pipeline configuration so it triggers a build on our chosen platform for both iOS and Android on a merge or tag push. 2) Configure the pipeline to use our already-configured credentials (App Store Connect API access and Play Console service account) without ever displaying, printing, or writing them into logs, code, or chat — just reference them as securely stored CI secrets/environment variables. 3) Add pipeline steps that upload the resulting build, version metadata, release notes, and screenshots to App Store Connect and to the Play Console via their respective upload mechanisms (fastlane deliver/supply or the platform's equivalent), describing each operation in plain language rather than raw API calls. 4) Include a step that runs basic validation (build succeeds, required metadata fields present) before submission. 5) Document the pipeline in a short README covering how to trigger it, where logs/status appear, and how to roll back a bad release. Done looks like: a working, version-controlled pipeline definition file, confirmation it runs end-to-end in a dry run or staging build, and the README. Report back with the pipeline file path, a summary of each stage, and any manual prerequisites (like initial account enrollment or secret storage) that remain a human step.

prod_012:n4.prompt:
You are helping me submit our mobile app for review in both App Store Connect and Google Play Console. Both listings and builds should already be staged; if you're missing any of the following, ask me first: (1) the app's bundle ID / package name, (2) confirmation the correct build number is uploaded and processed in both consoles, (3) confirmation that metadata, screenshots, privacy labels/data-safety forms, and pricing/availability are already filled in and saved, and (4) which release type we want (manual or phased release) for each store.

Using my configured credentials, please:

1. Log into App Store Connect, navigate to the app's version page, verify the build, export compliance, and metadata are all marked complete with no missing fields, then invoke the 'Submit for Review' action for that version.
2. Log into Google Play Console, navigate to the relevant release track (e.g., production or the track I specify), confirm the release notes, staged rollout percentage, and countries/regions are set as intended, then invoke the 'Submit for Review' / 'Start rollout' action to send the release to review.
3. Capture a screenshot or confirmation message from each console showing the submission was accepted and is now 'Waiting for Review' or equivalent status.

Done looks like: both consoles show the build in a review-pending state, with no blocking errors or missing-field warnings, and you have captured proof of submission from each.

Report back with: the review status shown in each console, the version/build numbers submitted, the submission timestamp, and screenshots or copied status text as evidence. Flag immediately if either console blocks submission due to missing information, since that would require me to supply additional details before resubmission.

prod_012:n5.prompt:
You are helping me monitor and manage the App Store and Google Play review process after I've submitted my app builds. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: (a) my Apple Developer account credentials access (via App Store Connect) and Google Play Console access — confirm I have these configured; (b) the app name/bundle ID or package name for both platforms; (c) the current build version numbers submitted for review.

2. Using my configured credentials, check App Store Connect and Google Play Console for the current review status of each submitted build. Log the status (Waiting for Review, In Review, Rejected, Approved, etc.) with timestamps.

3. If either platform shows a rejection, retrieve the full rejection reason/notes (App Store: Resolution Center messages and guideline references; Play Console: policy violation details) and summarize them clearly for me, including which guideline or policy was cited.

4. Draft a proposed response plan for any rejection: what metadata, screenshots, privacy labels, or binary changes would likely need to change, and draft any reply text needed for the Resolution Center. Do not resubmit, appeal, or reply on my behalf.

5. Set up a recurring check (e.g., poll every few hours or as often as your tools allow) until either app reaches an Approved/Live status or a new rejection appears, and report each status change to me as it happens.

Important: actually waiting on Apple's and Google's reviewer teams remains a human step — you cannot speed it up or influence reviewer judgment, only monitor and prepare responses. When you detect a status change (approval or rejection), report back to me immediately with: current status, any rejection details, and your drafted response/fix plan, then stop for human sign-off before any resubmission or Resolution Center reply is sent.

prod_012:n6.prompt:
You are helping me respond to an app store rejection (Apple App Store or Google Play Console) and prepare a resubmission. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the rejection notice text/screenshot or the specific rejection reason code and message from App Store Connect or Play Console, (2) my app's name, bundle ID/package name, and current version/build number, (3) links or access to my configured App Store Connect and/or Play Console accounts, and (4) any relevant privacy label, metadata, or screenshot files currently in the listing.

Once you have this, please:
1. Parse the rejection reason(s) and summarize in plain language what specifically was flagged (e.g., metadata mismatch, privacy label inaccuracy, broken functionality, guideline violation).
2. Draft a clear remediation plan listing exactly what needs to change — in the app binary, metadata, screenshots, privacy nutrition labels, or app description — to address each flagged issue.
3. Prepare updated listing copy, privacy label answers, or metadata fields as drafts (do not publish them).
4. Draft a professional resubmission note to the review team explaining what was changed and why, referencing the specific rejection reason.
5. Compile a checklist covering: code/binary fixes needed (if any), updated assets, updated metadata, and the drafted reviewer note.

Done looks like: a written summary of the rejection reason, a remediation checklist, drafted updated metadata/privacy label text, and a drafted resubmission note — all ready for me to review.

Do not submit, resubmit, publish changes, or confirm compliance on my behalf — deciding how to remediate and confirming the fix addresses the policy violation requires my judgment. Please prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off. Report back with the rejection summary, the remediation checklist, and all drafted text for my review.

prod_012:n7.prompt:
You are helping me finish shipping our mobile app: set up post-release monitoring for ratings, crashes, and performance in {{vendor}} (our observability tool) and mark the release event.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: our app's platform(s) (iOS/Android), the {{vendor}} account/API access we've configured, the app's package/bundle identifier, and the version/build number that just went live.

Actions to take:
1. In {{vendor}}, confirm (or create) the mobile app integration/agent config for our app so crash reports, ANRs, and performance traces are flowing.
2. Create alert rules for: crash-free session rate dropping below a sane threshold, spikes in errors/issues, and abnormal ANR or startup latency — with routing, grouping, and silencing configured so responders aren't spammed.
3. Verify errors are grouped into issues with stack traces, release tagging, and regression detection enabled so we can spot new-vs-recurring crashes.
4. Set up (or confirm) release/deploy tracking so crash and performance regressions can be correlated to this release.
5. Record this release as a deployment marker in {{vendor}} using its deployment-tracking command (e.g., `{{vendor}} deployment create`) with the version/build number, so the timeline shows exactly when it went live.
6. Query {{vendor}}'s GraphQL API (or dashboard) to pull a first-24-hours health summary: crash count, crash-free rate, top error groups, and any AI-generated incident summaries it offers.
7. Confirm you can jump from a trace/span to correlated logs and metrics for at least one sample request, to validate end-to-end debugging works.

Done looks like: alerts are live and correctly routed, the deployment marker is recorded, and you've produced a short health summary report (crash-free %, top issues, any anomalies) from {{vendor}}.

Report back with: what was configured, the alert rules created, the deployment marker confirmation, and the first health summary.
